ety.text: Clipping of periwig, itself an alteration of French perruque. The meaning of "to reprimand" perhaps came from this being something a bigwig would do or perhaps from the expressions to flip one's wig, wigs on the green, or dash my wig!

senses.d: A head of real or synthetic hair worn on the head to disguise baldness, for cultural or religious reasons, for fashion, or by actors to help them better resemble the character they are portraying.
ex: But wearing a wig is no reason to kill a man, with one or two notable exceptions.
Ye’ve been grossly deceived and put upon, Milly, and it’s my belief his old ruffian of an uncle in a wig is in the plot against us.

senses.d: To put on a wig; to provide with a wig (especially of an actor etc.).
To act in an extremely emotional way; to be overly excited, irritable, nervous, or fearful; behave erratically.
ex: That guy must be high. Look how he's wigging.

And I don't know nothin bout slippin
Zombie killer or rambo twinnin
Or a long pole like scaffold
Just tryna rise and aim and wig him

ety.text: Probably borrowed from western Lombard parrucca. Compare the phonetic changes of intervocalic -L- into -R- of Italian parlare and Sicilian parrari.

Uncertain; according to the OED, possibly related to Latin pilus (“hair”), but there are phonetic difficulties. It could instead be related to parrocchetto (“parakeet”), referring to the feathers. Compare its descendant French perruque and also Corsican and Sicilian pilucca and Romagnol piróca.
Borrowed from French perruque (influenced by pelo (“hair”)).

es:zorongo.gl: Andalusian dance style that emerged in the 17th or 18th century

ety.text: From French perruque, probably from Lombard perrucca from parrucca.
